headline: KC prop stocks surge 50% on minimal volume, while TPOLY consumer shares post a 12.5% price gap amid bondholder filing.
market_take: Property sector showed the widest swings today, led by KC up 50% on tiny volume and PF down 20% on higher volume. Consumer stocks were active with PLE up 16.7% and TPOLY posting a 12.5% opening gap; both also displayed intraday volatility. REITs and CONMAT saw several volume spikes and price gaps, but moves were modest. A cluster of filings – notably AKS delisting notice and TPOLY bondholder/financial‑risk disclosures – adds a layer of caution.

sector_notes.note: KC (+50.0%) and PF (-20.0%) dominate the day's moves; BROCK fell 12.5% on very high volume. AKS received a high‑severity trading‑sign filing warning of possible delisting, and GLAND issued a SET clarification request.

PLE rose 16.7% with a 40% intraday swing after a 16.7% opening gap; TPOLY opened +12.5% and also filed a bondholder‑meeting notice and a high‑risk financial transaction report. EMC displayed extreme volatility with a 50% gap and a 100% intraday jump.
CHOTI recorded a volume spike (4σ); XBIO opened down 14.29% then rallied 16.67% intraday, following a recent capital‑change filing. MADAME slipped 4.95% while KCG added 4.85%.

M‑STOR gained 7.38% on moderate volume. Multiple REITs (TNPF, MIPF, SIRIPRT) showed 100% price gaps, indicating possible suspension or corporate actions. PROSPECT filed a capital‑change notice on additional trust units.
DCC and GEL posted volume spikes and price gaps; GEL’s gap of -20% accompanied a 25% intraday rise.
UPOIC experienced a 100% opening gap, suggesting a potential trading halt.
